registered: 2026-11-03, before any run of the evaluator with --workers > 1; changing it needs a new ADR.
question: Do two concurrent Isaac worker processes give the same per-seed results as one, so --workers can change the wall time but never a verdict?

run.evaluator: piperobot.adapters.isaaclab.evaluate, one Isaac process per seed (ADR 0033), cuda:0

scripted_dev.covers: tcp actions through the differential IK

run.order: replay S, scripted_dev S, replay P, scripted_dev P; all at code_commit, on the same machine and driver. The S runs need no extra GPU memory and go first; the P runs go together once the precondition holds.
run.precondition: Before each P run, free GPU memory (total minus nvidia-smi memory.used) is at least 6.5 GB; otherwise the run waits. The free memory at each start is recorded.

pass_criteria: All four runs complete with exit 0 (infrastructure retries within the evaluator's own budget are allowed and reported).
For every one of the 125 seeds, S and P give the same outcome = (success, failure, success_step).
For every one of the 125 seeds, S and P give the same trajectory_sha256.
P's run_metadata records workers = 2 and S's records workers = 1.
failure_rule: Any other result fails the test: workers stay at 1 in the gate and the cause is investigated under a new registration. No run is repeated under this file.
predictions_not_criteria: replay S matches ADR 0033's acceptance run R1 on all 75 seeds (outcome and trajectory_sha256): 6/75 successes.
scripted_dev S matches the go/no-go's development run at 0bf1787 on these seeds (outcome and trajectory_sha256): 46/50 successes.
P's mean wall time per seed is at most 0.6 of S's (speedup >= 1.67x).
measured_no_threshold: Wall time per seed and the speedup, per set.
GPU memory: nvidia-smi memory.used sampled every 0.5 s during each run and for 30 s idle before it; idle = the median of that idle sample; peak above idle, for one worker (S) and for two (P).
Kit log files created during P runs: their count against the number of worker processes, and any name shared by two processes.
vram_constant: Reported to the gate as three numbers: S peak above idle, P peak above idle, and the per-worker constant = the larger of (S peak above idle) and (P peak above idle)/2, plus a 25% margin, rounded up to 256 MB.
